A1.justification: Despite the changed title and framing, both PDFs describe the same tree-search distraction framework and retain matching equations, experiments, and case studies. All 35 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, classifier experiments, ablations, mitigation results, and an 800-question human evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds mathematical-reasoning evaluation, classifier generalization tests, additional mitigation comparisons, and clean-accuracy measurements.

M1.justification: The classifier, error-guided generation, priority-queue search, value function, semantic and length checks, pruning, and DPO mitigation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix D. MATH-500 is preprocessed into the existing multiple-choice input format rather than introducing a different search algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains the four original QA benchmarks and adds MATH-500 mathematical reasoning, evaluated after conversion to multiple-choice questions (Appendix B.6). It also reports GSM-IC evaluation results in Appendix B.2, substantially extending the represented evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GSM-IC as a reported static-distraction comparator, few-shot CoT, in-context learning, and self-consistency mitigation comparisons, and SFT as a mitigation baseline against DPO (Tables 9, 11, and 13). Elaborated and Prompt-only are retained under the names ICA and SPD; their comparison values and underlying templates match v1.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include training the classifier on three datasets and testing on held-out TruthfulQA, generating three incorrect options with Claude-3.5-Sonnet for MATH-500, and measuring clean accuracy after DPO. Additional prompting configurations are evaluated. These extend the protocol substantially; the original main-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.4–B.7 add analyses of classifier transfer to an unseen dataset, sensitivity to alternative prompting strategies, whether DPO outperforms SFT, and whether robustness gains sacrifice clean accuracy. These address questions absent from v1. Existing value-function ablations, search-depth and length analyses, human validation, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five samples per search simulation and report point estimates. v2 adds no experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its additional tables retain the earlier reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 9–14 add substantial results for GSM-IC, held-out classifier evaluation, prompting strategies, MATH-500, SFT, and clean accuracy. For example, newly reported MATH-500 accuracy for GPT-4o is 0.813 before distraction and 0.488 afterward. Retained main tables keep their values. v2 also corrects the stated Claude-3.5-Sonnet accuracy drop from 49.5 to 38.4 percentage points, consistent with the unchanged 0.879 and 0.495 scores.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, value function, search and pruning equations, and mathematical assumptions are retained. The existing F-beta formula moves from the main text to Appendix B.1. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: v1 presents discovering a novel Contextual Distraction Vulnerability as a central contribution. v2 acknowledges prior research on that vulnerability and instead centers novelty on adaptive generation overcoming static evaluation methods. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion consequently redefine the principal contribution, while retaining the broad findings of substantial accuracy degradation and beneficial post-training mitigation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that the classifier captures dataset-independent susceptibility, distraction extends to tasks with explicitly evaluable correctness, and DPO preserves clean performance while improving robustness. Appendix E newly discusses evolving-model effectiveness and the restricted distraction types studied. These broaden applicability and tradeoff interpretations; the clean-performance claim understates the declines actually reported in Table 14.

D1.justification: The stated code repository changes from LLM_CDV to Adaptive_Distractions, without local evidence establishing a change in actual availability. v2 documents Claude-3.5-Sonnet generating three incorrect options for MATH-500. Existing model versions, hardware, learning rates, epochs, and prompt contents remain substantially unchanged; detailed configurations for several new comparisons are not supplied.

R1.justification: The broad vulnerability and tree-search review is replaced by an Appendix A organized around contextual robustness, perturbation generation, and mitigation. Added discussions include Shi et al.'s irrelevant-context work, Lost in the Middle, retrieval robustness, and PromptBreeder. This substantially changes the relationship to prior research and supports the revised novelty framing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial experimental discussion are rewritten, with terminology shifting from CDV to adaptive distraction. Related work and the overall algorithm move to appendices, and the appendix organization expands. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond the addition of experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, typography, table styling, and placement of displays. It adds six experimental tables, presents v1's tabular Figure 3 as Table 2, relocates Algorithm 1, and repacks retained case-study and prompt displays. Existing plots and case-study content are largely preserved rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The revised prior-work positioning and added generalization, prompting, SFT, and clean-accuracy evaluations make the paper better supported than v1. The net gain is limited by sparse setup details and overinterpretation: the GSM-IC contrast does not establish matched conditions, and Table 14 shows clean-accuracy declines despite claims of preservation, including Qwen2.5-7B falling from 0.480 to 0.411. The additions improve scrutiny of the central claims without fully resolving these evidential limitations.
